answer: Joint liability is the defence. A new agent to be graded must post a bond co-signed by an established agent, and that co-signer is liable for every identity it introduced. Onboarding is a bridge with one narrow runway a real counterparty must build. Flooding the chain with keys routes them to one wallet, so a confirmed fraud burns the branch, not just the clone. Ten thousand identities buy copies of one costly promise, each carrying the bond again, so attacker cost rises linearly while payoff is flat. That is a jetty paying where the tide reaches, a sable coat priced for pelts, not tags.
